excerpts:
# OAuth 2.0

OAuth 2.0 is a protocol that lets your app access a user’s account without accessing their password. Your app requests specific permission [scopes](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/scopes) and is granted an access token upon a user’s approval.

* A user will connect your app to one or more [tenants](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/auth-flow) . Depending on the API you’re using, a tenant can be a Xero organisation, a Xero HQ practice, or a Xero Practice Manager account.
* Apps using the code or PKCE flow can connect to a [maximum of 5 tenants](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/limits) . To connect to more than 5 tenants you need to upgrade to the [Core Tier](developer.xero.com/pricing) . Custom Connections can only ever connect to a single organisation.

## Choose the right authorization flow for your app

[](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/overview/)

Xero’s API supports the authorization code grant type using the standard [authorization code](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/auth-flow) flow or the [Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/pkce-flow) extension. We also have a premium integration option called [Custom Connections](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/custom-connections) which utilises the client credentials grant type.

|**Description** |**Code flow** |**PKCE flow** |**Custom Connection** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|Best for |Web server apps that can securely store a client secret. |Mobile and desktop apps that can’t securely store a client secret. (SPAs not currently supported). |Back end, machine-to-machine integrations. |
|Connection limit |5 connections on the [Starter Tier](developer.xero.com/pricing) |5 connections on the [Starter Tier](developer.xero.com/pricing) |One connection |
|Eligible for Marketplace |Yes |Yes |No |
|Offline Access |Yes |Yes |Yes |
|Cost |Free (Starter Tier) |Free (Starter Tier) |Monthly fee on the Xero organisation \- $10/m AUD inc GST \- $10/m NZD ex GST \- £5/m GBP ex VAT \- $5/m USD ex tax |
|Regional availability |Global |Global |UK, AU, NZ and US Xero organisations only |

excerpts:
Getting started

Can you give me an API key?

The Xero API does not support basic API Key authentication. Our API uses OAuth 2.0 which means you need to register your app to get a client id and client secret which you use to access the API.

How can I try out the API?

The quickest way to try out the API is to set up your demo company and dive into the API Explorer . Most of the API functionality is supported and you can quickly start playing with real calls against demo data.

How do I connect Xero to my Salesforce/SQL Database/thing you have no SDK for?

We've got SDKs to cover the most used technologies in the community, but we'll never cater for everyone. If we don't support your particular tech then check out our developer forum archive , or connect with other developers on Stack Overflow . You can also use our OpenAPI spec to generate your own SDK.

...

What Authentication do you support?

We currently support OAuth 1.0a and OAuth 2.0. However, OAuth 1.0a is in the process of being deprecated and OAuth 2.0 is required for all new integrations.

What kind of App should I build?

That's really up to you! Get connected with accountants and business owners to find out how you can help them be successful.

Granular Scopes

01. What changes are happening to scopes?

From 2 March 2026:
* Apps created before 2 March 2026 will have until September 2027 to move from broad scopes to granular scopes, however, we recommend updating as soon as possible. They’ll be available for you to request from April 2026. Once you start using granular scopes, your app will be able to use a mix of broad and granular scopes until all customers migrate to granular scopes by September 2027.
* Apps created on or after 2 March 2026 will use the new granular scopes

02. Why are there changes happening to scopes?

...

What should my agent do to avoid writing to the wrong organisation?

Always ask your agent to confirm with you before writing anything back to Xero. The server doesn't do this for you. For development, point the agent at the demo organisation and say that in its instructions.

What tools are available?

The full tool list with scopes is in the documentation .

What's the server URL?

api.xero.com/mcp/v1

Which MCP clients does it work with?

Any client that supports remote MCP servers. We've documented setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code.

Who can use it?

The Remote MCP is included on plans Core and above. Apps on the Starter plan can use it with the demo organisation only. See Xero Developer Pricing and Policies .

Why PKCE?

PKCE doesn't need a client secret, so there's no secret to leak into a prompt, a config file or an AI development tool.

results.title: Xero Developer Remote MCP — Xero Developer
excerpts:
Xero Developer Remote MCP

Connect an AI agent or client to Xero data and actions through a hosted URL: api.xero.com/mcp/v1 . Nothing to install, and you sign in with the same OAuth 2.0 flow you already use for the Xero API.

Overview

What is the Developer Remote MCP Server?

The Developer Remote MCP Server is a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server run by Xero. An MCP client, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor or an agent you’ve built, connects to it over a URL. Once connected, the AI agent or client can call Xero tools to read and write accounting data in organisations that have authorised your app.
It is recommended to use Xero’s existing OAuth 2.0 flow with PKCE . You don’t need separate credentials, and a PKCE app that works with the Xero API also works with the Remote MCP Server. Token type specifics remain the same.

Which clients does it work with?

Any client that supports the MCP standard. This includes Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and others.

Who can use it?

Remote MCP access is included for your Commercial App if you are on the Core plan or above, so there’s no extra charge for it. Data returned through the Remote MCP Server counts towards your plan’s data egress volume, the same as Xero API calls. Rate limits, connection counts and egress metering use the existing API limits.
Commercial Apps on the Starter plan can try out the Remote MCP Server with a demo organisation.
See Xero Developer Pricing and Policies .

...

Get started

Before you begin, you will need

* A Xero Developer account
* An app that uses PKCE and is on a plan that can access the Remote MCP Server. This is available for apps on the Core plan or above
* A Xero organisation to test against. Use a demo organisation if you’re on the Starter plan

Connect your agent

1. Create or open your app in the Xero Developer portal . When you create a Commercial app, choose PKCE as the authorisation method. Set the redirect URL per the required configuration of your MCP client. This will vary per client, so check its documentation.
2. Copy the Remote MCP Server URL: api.xero.com/mcp/v1
3. Add the URL to your MCP client as a remote server. The exact setting depends on the client, so check its documentation.
4. Start the agent and sign in when Xero prompts you.
5. Ask the agent to call get_connected_tenants . If it returns your organisation, you’re connected.

OAuth 2.0

OAuth 2.0 is a protocol that lets your app access a user’s account without accessing their password. Your app requests specific permission scopes and is granted an access token upon a user’s approval.
* A user will connect your app to one or more tenants . Depending on the API you’re using, a tenant can be a Xero organisation, a Xero HQ practice, or a Xero Practice Manager account.
* Apps using the code or PKCE flow can connect to a maximum of 25 tenants . To connect to more than 25 tenants you need to get your app certified . Custom Connections can only ever connect to a single organisation.

Choose the right authorization flow for your app

Xero’s API supports the authorization code grant type using the standard authorization code flow or the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension. We also have a premium integration option called Custom Connections which utilises the client credentials grant type.
* Description | Code flow | PKCE flow | Custom Connection
* Best for | Web server apps that can securely store a client secret. | Mobile and desktop apps that can’t securely store a client secret. (SPAs not currently supported). | Back end, machine-to-machine integrations.
* Connection limit | 25 connections (unlimited after certification) | 25 connections (unlimited after certification) | One connection
* Eligible for Marketplace | Yes | Yes | No
* Offline Access | Yes | Yes | Yes
* Cost | Free | Free | Monthly fee on the Xero organisation - $10/m AUD inc GST - $10/m NZD ex GST - £5/m GBP ex VAT - $5/m USD ex tax
* Regional availability | Global | Global | UK, AU, NZ and US Xero organisations only
The standard flow is the most well known OAuth 2.0 flow and typically used by web server applications. It requires your app to securely use and store a client secret.
The PKCE flow requires your app to create a secret (called a code verifier) for each authorization request. It’s slightly more complicated to implement but offers a secure way to connect to the API if your app can’t be trusted to store a client secret. Native (desktop and mobile) apps are required to use PKCE if connecting directly to the API.
Xero’s Custom Connections leverage the client_credentials grant type and are designed to make it easier to build bespoke integrations. Custom connections require less technical knowledge to build because Xero provides the authorisation flow. This means they’re also quicker to integrate and are easier to manage over time.

The standard authorization code flow

The standard authorization code flow is suitable for web server applications that can securely store a client secret. If you’re building a native app (desktop or mobile) then you should refer to the PKCE flow .
To get started, create an OAuth2 app and make sure you select the “Auth Code” grant type. Your app is assigned a unique Client ID and you can then generate a Client Secret. The Client Secret is private and should not be shared.

Xero tenants

Xero is a multi-tenanted platform with different types of tenants. Core Xero APIs (e.g. Accounting, Payroll, Files) operate within the context of an Organisation tenant but a tenant can also be a Practice Manager account or a XeroHQ practice. A user may have access to multiple tenants and will choose which ones to connect to your app. The type of tenant they can select will be determined by the scopes your app requests in the authorization step.
At the successful completion of an OAuth flow you will be granted an access token to act on behalf of the user. You will then use that access token to find out which tenants the user has connected to your app. From there, you can make API calls by providing both a valid access token and authorized tenant id with each request.

1. Send a user to authorize your app

Your app should direct users to the following url:
https: //login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOURCLIENTID&redirect_uri=YOURREDIRECTURI&scope=openid profile email accounting.invoices&state=123
copy code
The following values should be passed in as parameters:
* response_type=code
* client_id issued when you create your app
* scope permissions to request (see below)
* redirect_uri the URL on your server to redirect back to – This must be an https address, however for testing you can use localhost/ Please note that 127.0.0.1 cannot be used
* state a unique string to be passed back on completion (optional) (see below)

...

4. Receive your tokens

The token endpoint will verify all the parameters in the request, ensuring the code hasn’t expired and that the client ID and secret match. If everything checks out, it will generate your tokens and return them in the response.
It will contain the following parameters:
* access_token The token used to call the API.
* id_token The token containing user identity details (only returned if OpenID Connect scopes are requested).
* expires_in The amount of seconds until the access token expires.
* token_type: Bearer
* refresh_token The token used to refresh the access token once it has expired (only returned if the offline_access scope is requested).

Token expiry

All tokens received have an associated expiry time. Access tokens and refresh tokens can be exchanged prior to expiry.
Token expiry times:
* id_token: 5 minutes
* access_token: 30 minutes
* refresh_token: 60 days

The access token

...

6. Call the API

Make calls against the Xero APIs by simply adding the following headers to your request:
* Authorization : "Bearer " + access_token
* xero-tenant-id : tenantId
GET ../api.xro/ 2.0 /Invoices
 Authorization:  "Bearer "  + access_token
 Accept: application/json
 Xero-tenant-id:  45e4708 e-d862 -4111 -ab3a-dd8cd03913e1
copy code

Refreshing access and refresh tokens

Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. Your app can refresh an access token without user interaction by using a refresh token. You get a refresh token by requesting the offline_access scope during the initial user authorization. Refresh tokens expire after 60 days.
To refresh your access token you need to POST to the token endpoint:
https: //identity.xero.com/connect/token
copy code
The request will require an authorization header containing your app’s client_id and client_secret

excerpts:
Yes, apps on Starter plan can use it with the demo organisation. You can connect, run the tools, and decide whether it's worth upgrading to Core. Real customer organisations need the Core plan or above.

Can I use a web app instead of PKCE?

Technically yes. We don't recommend it. A web app's client ID and client secret are easy to paste into an AI-enabled tool by accident, and a PKCE app removes that risk.

Can I use the Remote MCP for free as an Accountant or Bookkeeper?

Yes. If you’re building an integration for your practice or a client, MCP access is included in your API fee exemption. To apply, go to Manage plan for your app in the Developer Portal and select Get in touch.

Do I need a Custom Connection?

No. Custom Connections apps are not eligible to access the Remote MCP Server.

Does a tool call run against one organisation or several?

One. Each call runs against a single organisation.

Does certification apply?

Certification rules haven't changed. Apps on Plus, Advanced and Enterprise must be certified, whether or not they use Remote MCP.

Does my client need to support OAuth?

Yes. The server authorises through Xero's OAuth 2.0 flow with PKCE, so your client needs to be able to start that flow.

Does the server ask the user to confirm before changing Xero data?

The tools on V1 do not elicit user confirmation. Always ask your agent to confirm with you before writing anything back to Xero.

results.title: Scopes — Xero Developer
excerpts:
# Scopes

When your app is requesting authorisation from a user it will need to ask for a set of scopes. These scopes will be displayed to the user and describe what data your app will be able to access.

## Scopes are additive

[](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/scopes/)

You should request the minimum scopes required for whatever action that user is performing. For example, if a user is doing single sign on you should only request the OpenID scopes. Later, if they want to connect to their Xero organisation you can request the additional scopes (e.g. accounting.transactions) by sending them through the [OAuth flow](developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/auth-flow) again. Each subsequent time your app sends a user through the flow, any new scopes will be added to previously consented scopes.

...

|Scope |Description |
| --- | --- |
|openid |your application intends to use the user’s identity |
|profile |first name, last name, full name and xero user id |
|email |email address |

...

### Payment services

|Scope |Description |Resources |
| --- | --- | --- |
|paymentservices |View and manage your payment services |[PaymentServices](developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/paymentservices) |

```
sources.title: The standard authorization code flow — Xero Developer
sources.trimmed:
# The standard authorization code flow

The standard authorization code flow is suitable for web server applications that can securely store a client secret. If you’re building a native app (desktop or mobile) then you should refer to the PKCE flow.

To get started, create an OAuth2 app and make sure you select the “Auth Code” grant type. Your app is assigned a unique Client ID and you can then generate a Client Secret. The Client Secret is private and should not be shared.

## Xero tenants

Xero is a multi-tenanted platform with different types of tenants. Core Xero APIs (e.g. Accounting, Payroll, Files) operate within the context of an Organisation tenant but a tenant can also be a Practice Manager account or a XeroHQ practice. A user may have access to multiple tenants and will choose which ones to connect to your app. The type of tenant they can select will be determined by the scopes your app requests in the authorization step.

At the successful completion of an OAuth flow you will be granted an access token to act on behalf of the user. You will then use that access token to find out which tenants the user has connected to your app. From there, you can make API calls by providing both a valid access token and authorized tenant id with each request.

## 1. Send a user to authorize your app

Your app should direct users to the following url:

```
https://login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOURCLIENTID&redirect_uri=YOURREDIRECTURI&scope=openid profile email accounting.invoices&state=123
```

The following values should be passed in as parameters:

* **response\_type=code**
* **client\_id** issued when you create your app
* **scope** permissions to request (see below)
* **redirect\_uri** the URL on your server to redirect back to – This must be an https address, however for testing you can use http://localhost/ Please note that http://127.0.0.1 cannot be used
* **state** a unique string to be passed back on completion (optional) (see below)

### Scopes

The scope parameter is a space-separated list of OAuth scopes, indicating what data you’d like your app to be able to access. You should request the minimum scopes required for whatever the user is doing at the time. The complete list of scopes can be found here.

### State

The state parameter should be used to avoid forgery attacks. Pass in a value that’s unique to the user you’re sending through authorisation. It will be passed back after the user completes authorisation.

## 2. Users are redirected back to you with a code

If the user authorizes your app, Xero will redirect back to your specified redirect\_uri with:

* **code** a temporary code that may only be exchanged once and expires 5 minutes after issuance.
* **state** (if you provided one). If the states don’t match, the request may have been created by a third party and you should abort the process.

If any errors occur or the user denies the request, we redirect back to your redirect\_uri with an error parameter.

## 3. Exchange the code

You can now exchange the verification code for an access token. You will also receive an identity token if you’ve requested OpenID Connect scopes and a refresh token if you’ve requested the offline\_access scope.

To do this you will need to make a POST request to our token endpoint:

```
https://identity.xero.com/connect/token
```

The request will require an authorization header containing your app’s client\_id and client\_secret

* **Authorization**: "Basic " + base64encode(client\_id + ":" + client\_secret)

The request body will need to contain the grant type (authorization\_code), code and redirect\_uri

* **grant\_type**=authorization\_code
* **code**=The authorization code you received in the callback
* **redirect\_uri**=The same redirect URI that was used when requesting the code

```
POST https://identity.xero.com/connect/token
authorization: "Basic " + base64encode(client_id + ":" + client_secret)
Content-Type: application/x-www-fo

sources.title: Remote MCP FAQs — Xero Developer
sources.trimmed:
## Remote MCP

### Can I connect to more than one organisation?

Yes. A user can authorise several organisations for the same app. Ask the agent to list the connected organisations, then tell it which one to act on. Each organisation still goes through the standard OAuth consent step.

### Can I see what my agent did?

Every Xero API call your agent makes is logged in the Developer Portal, under the app you own. Only the API calls are logged, not the tool calls or prompts behind them. If you need a record of what your agent asked for and why, you will need to log that in your own client or agent.

### Can I try it before I upgrade?

Yes, apps on Starter plan can use it with the demo organisation. You can connect, run the tools, and decide whether it's worth upgrading to Core. Real customer organisations need the Core plan or above.

### Can I use a web app instead of PKCE?

Technically yes. We don't recommend it. A web app's client ID and client secret are easy to paste into an AI-enabled tool by accident, and a PKCE app removes that risk.

### Can I use the Remote MCP for free as an Accountant or Bookkeeper?

Yes. If you’re building an integration for your practice or a client, MCP access is included in your API fee exemption. To apply, go to Manage plan for your app in the Developer Portal and select Get in touch.

### Do I need a Custom Connection?

No. Custom Connections apps are not eligible to access the Remote MCP Server.

### Does a tool call run against one organisation or several?

One. Each call runs against a single organisation.

### Does certification apply?

Certification rules haven't changed. Apps on Plus, Advanced and Enterprise must be certified, whether or not they use Remote MCP.

### Does my client need to support OAuth?

Yes. The server authorises through Xero's OAuth 2.0 flow with PKCE, so your client needs to be able to start that flow.

### Does the server ask the user to confirm before changing Xero data?

The tools on V1 do not elicit user confirmation. Always ask your agent to confirm with you before writing anything back to Xero.

### How do I disconnect an organisation or revoke access?

The user who authorized can disconnect access from their Connected Apps page
